sourceEvidence.title: Camshaft / Crankshaft Position Sensor Failure
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Diagnosis is done by scanning for correlation or sensor circuit codes and monitoring live RPM/cam signals during crank and road test. Repair usually involves replacing one or both cam sensors and sometimes the crank sensor, preferably with OE-quality parts because low-cost sensors often cause repeat faults. Typical repair cost is about $150-$450 depending on how many sensors are replaced and labor rates.

sourceEvidence.title: Radiator Crack and Coolant / Transmission Cross-Contamination
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Diagnosis includes checking the radiator and overflow bottle for oily residue, inspecting ATF for a milky appearance, and pressure-testing the cooling system. Repair typically requires replacing the radiator and thoroughly flushing the cooling and transmission systems; if contamination was severe, transmission repair or replacement may also be needed. Costs range from about $400 for early radiator replacement to $5,000+ if the transmission has been damaged.

sourceEvidence.title: Camshaft and Crankshaft Position Sensor Failure
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Diagnosis is done by scanning for cam/crank correlation or sensor circuit faults and monitoring RPM/cam signals during cranking. Repair usually involves replacing the failed camshaft sensor(s) and/or crankshaft sensor with quality OEM-equivalent parts and clearing codes; access is generally straightforward compared with internal engine work. Typical repair cost is about $180 to $500 depending on how many sensors are replaced.

sourceEvidence.title: Camshaft and Crankshaft Position Sensor Failure
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Scan for stored fault codes and monitor cam/crank synchronization data while checking harness condition near the sensors. Repair typically involves replacing the failed camshaft position sensor(s) and sometimes the crankshaft position sensor with quality parts, then clearing codes and confirming proper restart behavior. Using OEM-supplier sensors is strongly preferred because cheap sensors often cause repeat failures.

sourceEvidence.title: Camshaft / Crankshaft Position Sensor Failure
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Diagnosis is done with a scan tool and live data to identify which sensor is dropping out, followed by checking connector condition and harness integrity. Repair involves replacing the failed camshaft or crankshaft position sensor with a quality OE-equivalent part and clearing codes; typical repair costs range from about $180-$450 depending on which sensor failed and labor access.

sourceEvidence.title: Radiator / Cooling Fan Module Failure
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Diagnosis includes pressure-testing the cooling system, checking for seepage at radiator end tanks, and commanding fan operation with a scan tool. Repairs usually involve replacing the radiator and/or fan assembly, refilling with the correct Nissan/Infiniti blue coolant, and bleeding the system; typical cost ranges from about $700 to $1,800 depending on which components fail.

sourceEvidence.title: Power Steering Pump Whine
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Flush the power steering system and refill with Nissan PSF. Bleed air from the system by turning the wheel lock-to-lock several times with the engine running. Replace the pump if the noise persists after fluid service.
